principles: A short charge to a son already doing well

world_behind.title: Shiblon went to Antionum
world_behind.text: Alma 31:7 named him among those Alma took to the Zoramites. Verses 3 and 4 refer to what happened to him there, and the record gives that history only here.

world_behind.title: He was jailed and stoned
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says he was in bonds and stoned for the word's sake. Nothing in Alma 31 through 35 mentions it; Alma supplies the detail privately to the son it happened to.

world_behind.title: This is the shortest of the three charges
world_behind.text: Fifteen verses, against thirty for Helaman's first and forty-seven for his second. Alma has less to correct and says so.

world_behind.title: The conversion account is compressed
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 give the angel, the three days, and the cry for mercy in two verses. Alma 36 spent twenty-four on the same material.

world_behind.title: The Zoramite prayer is still in view
world_behind.text: Verses 13 and 14 tell Shiblon how not to pray, using the Rameumptom as the example. He was standing there when it was offered.

world_behind.title: The instructions are mostly about restraint
world_behind.text: Not lifted up, not boasting, not overbearing, bridle the passions, refrain from idleness. The list is almost entirely about what to hold back.

world_behind.title: The farewell matches Helaman's
world_behind.text: Verse 15 ends with teaching the word, being sober, and farewell, the same three items that close Alma 37.

words.text: Constancy, holding a course. The word appears four times in this record and never in the King James Bible. Alma names it first among Shiblon's qualities, and Alma 39 opens by asking Corianton whether he has observed the steadiness of his brother.
Acute distress of body or mind. The record uses it eleven times and the King James Bible seventeen. Alma pairs it with bitter pain to cover three days in one phrase, where Alma 36 needed six verses.

Moderate, self-restrained. The record uses it twice and the King James Bible three times, always in lists of qualities expected of a teacher. Alma 7 has the same word in a longer list Alma gave publicly at Gideon.
Domineering force in speech or manner. The word occurs once in scripture. Alma pairs it against boldness in the same clause, which makes it the excess of a quality he is asking his son to keep.

To fit with a bridle, to control as a horse is controlled. The record uses it once and the King James Bible nine times, including James on bridling the whole body. Alma applies it to the passions and attaches a purpose: that ye may be filled with love.

The state of not deserving. The word appears three times in this record and never in the King James Bible. Alma makes acknowledging it the substance of the prayer he wants, in place of the thanksgiving the Zoramites offered.

phrases.term: Even as I said unto Helaman
phrases.text: Alma opens by telling one son what he told the other. The promise is identical to Alma 36:1 and 37:13, and he repeats it word for word so that Shiblon knows the family standard is the same.

phrases.term: Blessed is he that endureth to the end
phrases.text: Alma's hope for a son who has already started well. He credits Shiblon with commencing in his youth and puts the blessing on continuing.

phrases.term: I also know that thou wast stoned for the word's sake
phrases.text: The one place the record mentions this. Alma names it, says his son bore it with patience, and credits the Lord with the deliverance, without describing anything further.

phrases.term: As much as ye shall put your trust in God even so much ye shall be delivered
phrases.text: A proportional promise. Alma states the relation as a measure, and applies it to trials, troubles, and afflictions in that order.

phrases.term: I did cry unto him and I did find peace to my soul
phrases.text: The conversion in ten words. Alma 36 gave the same event at length; here the cry and the peace sit in one clause, and verse 9 says why he is telling it.

phrases.term: There is no other way or means whereby man can be saved, only in and through Christ
phrases.text: The reason Alma gives for retelling his own story. Nephi says the same in 2 Nephi 31 and Peter says it before the Sanhedrin, and Alma offers it as the lesson the story exists to carry.
Six words containing the chapter's method. Alma keeps the quality and names its excess, which is how the rest of the verse works too: passions bridled so that love can fill, idleness refused.

phrases.term: See that ye bridle all your passions, that ye may be filled with love
phrases.text: The restraint has a stated purpose. Alma does not ask for passions to be removed; the bridling is what makes room for something else.

phrases.term: Do not pray as the Zoramites do, for ye have seen that they pray to be heard of men
phrases.text: Alma appeals to something his son witnessed. Shiblon stood at Antionum and watched the Rameumptom, and the instruction is built on that memory.

phrases.term: O Lord, forgive my unworthiness, and remember my brethren in mercy
phrases.text: The prayer Alma supplies in place of the Zoramite one. It reverses both halves: unworthiness for chosenness, and mercy for the brethren in place of thanks that they are damned.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: The same promise
verses.text: Keep the commandments and prosper; break them and be cut off, exactly as said to Helaman. Alma trusts he will have joy in Shiblon because of his steadiness, and hopes he will continue, since the blessing is on enduring to the end.

verses.label: v. 3–5
verses.title: What he endured
verses.text: Alma has already had joy in him for his faithfulness, diligence, patience, and long-suffering among the Zoramites. He was in bonds and was stoned for the word's sake, and bore it because the Lord was with him. Trust in God and be delivered in proportion.

verses.label: v. 6–8
verses.title: The conversion, short
verses.text: Alma disclaims knowing these things of himself. An angel was sent to stop his work of destruction, with a voice like thunder that shook the earth. Three days and nights of bitter pain and anguish, and no remission until he cried to Christ, and then peace.

verses.label: v. 9–12
verses.title: What to do
verses.text: Learn that there is no other way to be saved except through Christ, who is the life and the light of the world. Continue teaching, be diligent and temperate, avoid pride and boasting, use boldness without overbearance, bridle the passions, refuse idleness.

verses.label: v. 13–14
verses.title: How not to pray
verses.text: Do not pray as the Zoramites, who pray to be heard of men and praised for their wisdom. Do not thank God that you are better than your brethren. Ask forgiveness for your unworthiness and mercy for them, and acknowledge it at all times.

verses.label: v. 15
verses.title: The blessing
verses.text: May the Lord bless your soul and receive you into his kingdom to sit down in peace. Go teach the word to this people. Be sober. Farewell.

chapter.title: The shortest charge goes to the son doing best
chapter.text: Fifteen verses, and most of them are commendation and general instruction. Alma spends his length where it is needed, and Alma 39 shows where that is.

chapter.title: A son's suffering is on the record only because his father named it
chapter.text: Bonds and stoning at Antionum appear nowhere in the mission account. The private charge is where it is preserved.

chapter.title: The conversion is retold as an argument
chapter.text: Verse 9 says why: so Shiblon may learn there is no other way to be saved. The story is offered as evidence rather than as memoir.

chapter.title: The virtues are named with their excesses
chapter.text: Boldness against overbearance, passion against bridling, diligence against idleness. Alma teaches by marking the edge of each quality, so his son can tell when he has passed it.

chapter.title: Bridling is for filling
chapter.text: The purpose clause matters: passions are controlled so that love can fill the person. The restraint is presented as making room.

chapter.title: The counter-prayer is exact
chapter.text: The Rameumptom thanked God for election and for others being cast down. Alma's version asks forgiveness for the self and mercy for the brethren, reversing both clauses.

chapter.title: He cites what his son saw
chapter.text: Alma does not describe Zoramite worship. He says ye have seen, because Shiblon was there, and lets the memory carry the instruction.

chapter.title: The three charges share a closing
chapter.text: Teach the word, be sober, farewell. Alma 37 and Alma 38 end with the same three, which makes the difference in Alma 42's ending visible when it comes.

applications.title: Tell someone what you have noticed about them
applications.text: Alma listed four things his son had done well before instructing him at all. Pick someone steady in your life and name specifically what you have seen.

applications.title: Keep the quality and name the excess
applications.text: Alma asked for boldness without overbearance. Take a strength of yours and work out what its excess looks like, so you can tell when you have crossed into it.

applications.title: Bridle rather than remove
applications.text: The purpose of the control is to be filled with love. When you are trying to master something in yourself, decide what the restraint is making room for.

applications.title: Write the opposite prayer
applications.text: Alma gave his son the exact reversal of the prayer he had heard. Take a way of thinking you know is wrong and compose the sentence that inverts it.

questions.text: What have I commenced in that I have not continued?
What have I borne patiently that nobody else knows about?
Have I trusted God in proportion to the deliverance I expect?
Could I say in one sentence why I believe what I believe?
Where does my boldness turn into overbearance?
Whose approval am I actually praying toward?
When did I last ask God to remember someone else in mercy?
